Compressed sensing methods with applications to advanced air sampling Cassidy Campbell Office of Science, Science Undergraduate Laboratory Internship Program Florida Polytechnic University Savannah River National Laboratory Aiken, South Carolina 07-17-2025 Prepared in partial fulfillment of the requirement of the Department of Energy, Office of Science’s Science Undergraduate Laboratory Internship Program under the direction of Steve Chiswell at the Savannah River National Laboratory. Participant: Cassidy Campbell Research Advisor: Steve Chiswell 1 ABSTRACT Environmental sampling methods developed by the Savannah River National Laboratory (SRNL) employ collectors with sorbent media tubes set at various locations to collect airborne emissions. Laboratory analyses of these tubes results in one-dimensional signals regarding what chemicals are being released and transported within the atmosphere. The analysis process is time consuming especially when analyzing a full year’s worth of tubes (hourly sample collection results in nearly 9,000 tubes per year). Using a signal processing method such as compressed sensing allows for recreation of the full signal while greatly reducing the number of analyzed samples required. Due to the sparsity of data retrieved from the air tubes, it is possible to use measurements a fraction of the size of the original data to gain much of the same information. This would improve the overall time and cost of analysis when modeling one-dimensional sampling signals. I. INTRODUCTION Compressed sensing is a recent addition to applied mathematics research which provides an advanced method of one-dimensional signal compression and reconstruction. By assuming the original signal is sparse in some domain (contains very few non-zero values) and compressible1 we are able to create a linear system of equations to compress the signal. We hypothesize it is possible to take a limited number of random samples from some sparse vector derived from the original signal and reconstruct a full signal of the original’s size.
